# Protocol

Binding description of the interface between the app (`src/crypto/`, `src/sync/`) and the
server (`server/`). Every change affects both sides: record it here and note it in the section
"Changes". The test vectors in `server/testdata/vectors.json` (generated by
`server/testdata/gen-vectors.mjs`) are part of the protocol. Go and Vitest tests check against
them.

Status: **binding** (since 2026-11-23)

## 1. Basic rules

- All paths under `/api/v1`. JSON in `camelCase`. Binary data as Base64url without padding.
- Times as Unix milliseconds, always set by the server.
- Auth via header `Authorization: Bearer <sessionToken>`. WebSocket via query `?token=` when
  connecting (browsers cannot set headers on a WebSocket), never afterwards.
- CORS: only the configured app origins are allowed (`APP_ORIGINS`, comma-separated:
  production `https://tablegrade.pages.dev` and dev preview `https://dev.tablegrade.pages.dev`).
  `RP_ID` for passkeys is `tablegrade.pages.dev`; the dev preview may use this RP ID as its
  parent domain, so passkeys work for both. The app runs with COEP `require-corp`, so it loads
  photos via `fetch`, not via `<img src>`.
- Errors: HTTP status plus `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<German, for the UI>" }`.
  Codes: `unauthorized`, `session_revoked`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `too_large`,
  `rate_limited`, `upgrade_required`, `bad_request`.
- Further codes: `gone` (410, see 4), `server_restored` (410, see 4), `forbidden` (403),
  `not_approved` (403, account not approved yet, see 2), `internal` (500, server error).
- Status per code: `bad_request` 400, `unauthorized` 401, `session_revoked` 401,
  `forbidden` 403, `not_found` 404, `conflict` 409, `gone` 410, `server_restored` 410,
  `too_large` 413, `upgrade_required` 426, `rate_limited` 429 (with header `Retry-After` in
  seconds).
- Every response carries `X-Protocol-Version: 1`. The client sends the same header. If the
  client sends a higher major version than the server knows: `upgrade_required`.
- Texts (labels, AAD, HMAC inputs) are always UTF-8. `‖` means concatenating bytes.
- HKDF is always HKDF-SHA256 with 32 bytes of output. `salt=""` means an empty salt
  (WebCrypto: `new Uint8Array(0)`, equivalent to 32 zero bytes per RFC 5869).
- AES-256-GCM always with a 12-byte nonce and a 16-byte tag. Format everywhere
  `nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext ‖ tag(16)` (WebCrypto returns `ciphertext ‖ tag` in one piece).
- Crockford Base32: alphabet `0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ`, bits from the front (MSB
  first), no padding. Input normalization: remove spaces and `-`, upper case, `O`→`0`, `I` and
  `L`→`1`. `U` and other characters are invalid.

## 2. Accounts, identities, sessions

Data model on the server (extensible for org customers, see the concept):

```
users       id (uuid), createdAt, customerId? (later), deletedAt?
identities  userId, provider ('passkey' | 'microsoft' | 'google'), subject, createdAt
passkeys    userId, credentialId, publicKey, signCount, transports, prfCapable, name, createdAt
devices     id (uuid), userId, name, createdAt, lastSeenAt, revokedAt?
sessions    tokenHash, userId, deviceId, createdAt, lastUsedAt, expiresAt
keyWraps    id, userId, kind ('passkey' | 'recovery' | 'org'), credentialId?, alg, wrapped, createdAt
```

- A session token is 32 random bytes. The server stores only its SHA-256.
- A session belongs to exactly one device. It expires after 90 days without use. Every use
  extends it.
- `devices.revokedAt` set → all sessions of the device return `session_revoked`.

### Endpoints

| Method, path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /auth/passkey/register/begin` | Options for a new account or another passkey (with session). Requests the PRF extension. |
| `POST /auth/passkey/register/finish` | Store the passkey. Without session: new account plus session. |
| `POST /auth/passkey/login/begin` | Options for the sign-in (discoverable credentials). |
| `POST /auth/passkey/login/finish` | Verify, create a session. |
| `GET  /auth/oidc/{provider}/config` | Client id, authorize URL, scopes for the browser. |
| `POST /auth/oidc/{provider}/exchange` | Body: `code`, `codeVerifier`, `redirectUri`, `deviceName`. The server exchanges the code, verifies the ID token, creates an account if needed, returns a session. |
| `GET  /auth/session` | Session check: `{ userId, deviceId, identities[], devices[], approved, contactEmail, accessNote, rpId }`. `rpId` is the WebAuthn RP ID; the app needs it for passkey requests without a server ceremony (unlocking via PRF), because the dev preview runs on a subdomain. |
| `POST /auth/logout` | End the session. |
| `GET  /devices` / `POST /devices/{id}/revoke` / `PATCH /devices/{id}` | List, revoke, rename devices. |
| `PUT  /account/contact` | Body `{ email, note }`: contact address and reason of the access request. Empty values delete. Response `204`. |
| `DELETE /account` | Delete the account with all data (after confirmation in the UI). Response `204`; connected devices get `revoked` via WebSocket, their sessions are invalid afterwards (`unauthorized`). |
| `POST /auth/dev/login` | Only with `DEV_AUTH=1` (tests). Body `{ deviceName, userId? }`. Without `userId` a new account, with `userId` another device of this account. Response like every sign-in. |

Response of a successful sign-in:
`{ "sessionToken", "userId", "deviceId", "isNewUser" }`. `sessionToken` is Base64url.

- `register/begin` and `login/begin` return `{ challengeId, options }`. `options` are the
  WebAuthn options in JSON format (`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` or
  `…RequestOptionsJSON`, binary fields Base64url). `finish` gets
  `{ challengeId, credential, deviceName }`, `credential` via `toJSON()`. A challenge is valid
  for 5 minutes and only once.
- `register/finish` stores `prfCapable = true` if the client reports
  `clientExtensionResults.prf.enabled = true` (or already returns `prf.results` there).
- `begin` gets the body `{}`. With an `Authorization` header, `register/*` is for another
  passkey of the account; an invalid token returns `unauthorized` (never a new account).
  `register/finish` with a session responds `204`; `deviceName` is then only the passkey's
  label. More than 20 passkeys: `conflict`.
- The WebAuthn user id (`user.id`) is the UTF-8 encoding of the `userId`.
- The options of both `begin` calls already contain `extensions.prf.eval.first` = Base64url of
  the PRF salt (see 3). Options require `residentKey: required`.
- Every failed passkey verification returns `401 unauthorized`; an expired or already used
  challenge returns `400 bad_request`.
- Device: every new session without an existing session creates a new device with
  `deviceName`.
- `GET /auth/oidc/{provider}/config` returns
  `{ clientId, authorizeUrl, scopes: ["openid", "email"], redirectUri }`. The browser uses
  PKCE (`S256`) and `state`; only the browser checks both. It sends `prompt=select_account`,
  so that after signing out in the app the account picker appears instead of the same account
  right away.
- `{provider}` is `microsoft` or `google`. A provider without a client id is off:
  `404 not_found`. `redirectUri` belongs to the app origin from the `Origin` header (otherwise
  the first one of `APP_ORIGINS`). `exchange` only accepts these redirect URIs, otherwise
  `bad_request`.
- An account has exactly one sign-in method (Microsoft or Google). `exchange` with a session
  therefore responds `409 conflict`; to switch, sign out. Without a session: sign-in or new
  account, response like every sign-in, plus `email` (claim `email`, missing without the
  claim). The device shows it as "Angemeldet als …" and stores it only locally. Rejected code
  or invalid ID token: `401 unauthorized`.
- Identity: `subject` is the claim `sub` for OIDC (Google) or `sub` with tenant `consumers`
  (Microsoft), for passkeys the `credentialId` (Base64url). The server neither stores nor logs
  email or name.
- **Approval:** a new account has `approved: false`. Sign-in, `GET /auth/session`, logout,
  devices, `PUT /account/contact` and `DELETE /account` work. Keys, records, photos, device
  link and WebSocket respond `403 not_approved`. The operator approves accounts with a command
  on the server (`notenfeder-server admin approve`, see `server/README.md`). Accounts from
  before this change count as approved. Test sign-ins (`DEV_AUTH`) as well.
- **Contact:** `email` is a plain address (without display name, at most 254 characters),
  `note` at most 500 characters. Purpose: approval, maintenance, payment. Both are stored in
  plaintext on the server (an exception to the "ciphertext only" principle, for this purpose)
  and are deleted with the account. In `GET /auth/session` an empty value is `null`.
- The app signs in only with Microsoft or Google. It creates passkeys only with a session, for
  unlocking. The server still offers sign-in and new accounts via passkey; the app does not use
  them.
- `GET /auth/session`: `identities` = `[{ provider, createdAt }]` (without `subject`),
  `devices` as in `GET /devices`. `POST /auth/logout`, `PATCH /devices/{id}` and
  `POST /devices/{id}/revoke` respond `204` without a body. Device names: 1–80 characters,
  surrounding spaces are removed.
- `GET /devices` returns
  `{ devices: [{ id, name, createdAt, lastSeenAt, revokedAt, current }] }`.
  `PATCH /devices/{id}` with `{ name }`. A device cannot revoke itself (`conflict`); `logout`
  is for that.

Microsoft: tenant `consumers` (personal accounts only). Google: a normal OAuth client id of
type "Web application". The redirect URI is the app origin with path `/`, without query
(Microsoft rejects redirect URIs with a query). The app recognizes the return by `state` plus
`code` or `error`.

## 3. Keys

| Name | Content |
|---|---|
| DEK | Data key, AES-256-GCM, 32 random bytes, one per account. |
| IDK | Id key, `HKDF-SHA256(DEK, salt="", info="notenfeder/record-id/v1")`, HMAC-SHA256. |
| Wrap | AES-256-GCM encryption of the 32 DEK bytes with a KEK, AAD = `notenfeder/wrap/v1/<kind>/<userId>`. Format: `nonce(12) ‖ ciphertext+tag`. |

KEK per kind:

- **passkey:** PRF output (32 bytes) for the fixed salt `SHA-256("notenfeder/prf/v1")`, then
  `HKDF-SHA256(prf, salt="", info="notenfeder/kek/passkey/v1")`. One wrap per passkey
  (`credentialId`). Passkeys without PRF only serve for sign-in.
- **recovery:** 20 random bytes (160 bits). KEK = `HKDF-SHA256(bytes, salt="",
  info="notenfeder/kek/recovery/v1")`. No slow KDF needed, the entropy is high enough.
  Text: 32 characters Crockford Base32 of the bytes, then 4 check characters = the first
  20 bits of `SHA-256("notenfeder/recovery/v1" ‖ bytes)` as Crockford Base32. 36 characters in
  total, shown in 9 groups of four with `-`, e.g. `K7QF-M2XA-…`. Input: normalize (see 1),
  check length 36, check the check characters. Wrong check characters → message
  "Tippfehler im Schlüssel", without a server request.
- **org:** later (the school's master key, public key). The `alg` format leaves room.

- A wrap as JSON: `{ id, kind, credentialId?, alg, wrapped, createdAt }`. `id` is a UUID from
  the client. `alg` is `"A256GCM"` for passkey and recovery. `wrapped` is Base64url.
- Each account has at most one `recovery` wrap. A new recovery key replaces the old one (`PUT`
  with a new `id`, then `DELETE` of the old one).

| Method, path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /keys` | All wraps of the account: `{ keys: [ … ] }`. |
| `PUT /keys/{id}` | Create or replace a wrap (e.g. new passkey, new recovery key). |
| `DELETE /keys/{id}` | Delete a wrap. The last `recovery` wrap cannot be deleted. |

- `PUT` and `DELETE` respond `204`. `{id}` is a lower-case UUID; an `id` in the body must be
  equal (it may be missing). The server sets `createdAt`.
- `PUT` checks: `kind` is `passkey` or `recovery` (`org` follows later), `alg` is `A256GCM`,
  `wrapped` has exactly 60 bytes. `passkey` needs a `credentialId` of a passkey of this
  account, `recovery` none. Otherwise `bad_request`. If the `id` belongs to another account:
  `conflict`.
- `DELETE` of the last `recovery` wrap: `conflict`. Unknown `id`: `not_found`.

## 4. Records

```
records  userId, id, seq, updatedAt, deleted, schema, ciphertext, deviceId
```

- `id` = Base64url of `HMAC-SHA256(IDK, "<table>|<primary key>")`, truncated to 16 bytes
  (22 characters). The primary key is the UUID, or for composite keys the values in schema
  order, separated by `|`. Numbers (`SchoolYears.year`) as decimals without leading zeros.
  UUIDs in lower case. `<table>` is the SQL name (e.g. `Classes`). So the id reveals neither
  table nor date.
- The server assigns `seq`, strictly increasing per account.
- Plaintext before encryption:
  `{ "t": "<table>", "k": [<primary key>], "v": <schema version>, "row": { … } | null }`.
  `row: null` for a deletion.
- `row` contains all columns with their SQL names and values as in SQLite (text, number,
  `null`). The plaintext is UTF-8 JSON; the order of the fields does not matter.
- Encryption: AES-256-GCM with the DEK, 12 random bytes nonce,
  AAD = `notenfeder/record/v1/<userId>/<id>`. `ciphertext` = `nonce ‖ ciphertext+tag`, in
  JSON as Base64url.
- `schema` = version of the local DB (like `BASELINE_VERSION + migrations`), unencrypted, so
  that an old device recognizes newer records and holds them back.

| Method, path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /records/push` | Body: `{ records: [{ id, deleted, schema, ciphertext, blobs }] }`, max. 500 records or 5 MB. Response: `{ results: [{ id, seq, updatedAt }] }` in the same order. Last write wins: the new record always replaces the old one. The same id twice in one push: the last one wins. |
| `GET /records/pull?after=<seq>&limit=<n>` | Records with `seq > after`, ascending, max. 1000 (default 500). Response `{ records: [{ id, seq, updatedAt, deleted, schema, ciphertext, deviceId }], more, latestSeq }`. |

- Push: the 5 MB apply to the whole request body (otherwise `too_large`). 0 or more than 500
  records, an `id` or blob id that is not 16 bytes Base64url, `schema` < 1, a `ciphertext`
  under 28 bytes or more than 16 blobs per record: `bad_request`. At most 60 pushes per minute
  and account (`rate_limited`).
- Pull: `after` and `limit` are integers ≥ 0 and ≥ 1, otherwise `bad_request`. A `limit` above
  1000 counts as 1000. `after=0` never gets `gone`.
- If `after` is greater than `latestSeq`, a server backup was restored. Response: `410` with
  code `server_restored`. The device wins: it uploads **all** local synced rows again (as when
  first turned on) and then fetches everything from `after=0`. If two devices have different
  states, the one syncing last wins (accepted on purpose).
- Deletions carry a `ciphertext` as well (plaintext with `row: null`). So the key `k` stays
  readable for the device applying the deletion.
- The server also sends a device its own records back. The client recognizes them by
  `deviceId` and skips them if nothing newer for the key is in `_outbox`.

Tombstones stay at least 180 days. A device that was offline longer (`after` older than the
oldest kept deletion) gets `410 gone` and then loads everything again (`after=0`). The server
may remove deleted records with a `seq` older than 180 days; it remembers the highest removed
`seq` per account as the limit for `gone`.

### Synced tables

All tables from `src/db/schema.ts` except:

- `Holidays` (cache of the holiday API, each device loads it itself),
- entries in `Settings` that concern only the device (`DEVICE_SETTING_KEYS` in
  `src/lib/settings.ts`): `holidayCache`, `lastBackup`, `pinHash`, `colorMode`,
  `compactTable`, `compactTimetable`. The settings tab and the display options live in
  `localStorage` and are not in the DB anyway.

Primary keys per table (the order applies to `pk` and `k`): `Classes`, `Students`, `Grades`,
`Traits`, `Duties`: `id`; `Classes2Students`: `classId, studentId`; `Students2Traits`:
`studentId, traitId`; `CancelledDays`: `date`; `CancelledLessons`: `classId, date`;
`LessonTypes`: `classId, date, type`; `Reports`: `classId, date, kind`; `ReportGrades`:
`classId, date, kind, studentId`; `SchoolYears`: `year`; `Settings`: `key`.

Local capture (migration 23): on INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, triggers write
`(tbl, pk = JSON array of the key, changedAt in ms)` to `_outbox` if
`_sync_state.enabled = '1'` and `_sync_state.applying != '1'`. If an UPDATE changes the key,
the old key is captured as well (sent as deleted). Cascades via foreign keys fire the triggers
too. When sending, the sync engine reads the current row for the key; if it is missing, it
sends a deletion.

The internal table `_outbox` and sync tables (`_sync_*`) are never synced.

## 5. Photos

- Photos stay locally as data URLs in `Students.image`.
- Image data = the UTF-8 bytes of the complete data URL (`data:image/…;base64,…`). So the
  image type is kept.
- When syncing, the engine replaces `image` in the plaintext with `{ "blob": "<blobId>" }`.
  `blobId` = Base64url of `HMAC-SHA256(IDK, "blob|" ‖ SHA-256(image data))` (hash as 32 raw
  bytes), truncated to 16 bytes.
- The photo itself: AES-256-GCM with the DEK, AAD = `notenfeder/blob/v1/<userId>/<blobId>`.
  Uploaded is `nonce ‖ ciphertext+tag` as `application/octet-stream`.

| Method, path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `PUT /blobs/{blobId}` | Upload (max. 2 MB). If the blob exists already: `200` without change. |
| `GET /blobs/{blobId}` | Download. |

- `PUT` responds `201` for a new blob, `200` for an existing one (the body is then ignored).
  `blobId` must be 16 bytes Base64url, the body at least 28 bytes (`bad_request`), at most
  2 MB (`too_large`).
- `GET` returns the bytes as `application/octet-stream` with
  `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`. Foreign or unknown ids: `not_found`.
- An uploaded blob without a reference counts as orphaned from the upload on. The client
  therefore pushes the record within 30 days after the upload.

The server deletes blobs no record has referenced for 30 days. For this the client reports
the blob references in the plaintext field `blobs: [<blobId>]` per record when pushing (the
server only sees the ids).

## 6. Device link

1. The new device (signed in, but without DEK) creates an ECDH P-256 key pair and calls
   `POST /link` with its public key. Response: `{ linkId, code }`. `code` = 8 characters
   Crockford Base32 (40 random bits from the server), valid for 10 minutes. Public keys always
   in raw format (uncompressed point, 65 bytes, `0x04 ‖ x ‖ y`), in JSON as Base64url.
2. The new device shows the `code`.
3. The old device (with DEK) enters the `code`, fetches `GET /link/by-code/{code}` →
   `{ linkId, publicKey }`.
4. The old device immediately sends `POST /link/{linkId}/key` with `{ publicKey }` (`pubOld`).
   The new device gets it via `GET /link/{linkId}` (`status: "keyed"`) or via WebSocket. Both
   devices then show a **check code**: the first 4 bytes of `SHA-256(pubNew ‖ pubOld)` as an
   unsigned number (big endian) modulo 1 000 000, padded with leading zeros to 6 digits. The
   user confirms on the old device that both are equal; only then step 5 follows. The new
   device takes over the DEK only after its own confirmation.
5. The old device derives a key via ECDH (shared secret = x coordinate, 32 bytes) plus
   `HKDF(secret, salt="", info="notenfeder/link/v1")`, wraps the DEK as in 3 with
   `kind = link` (AAD `notenfeder/wrap/v1/link/<userId>`) and sends
   `POST /link/{linkId}/complete` with `{ publicKey, wrapped }`.
6. The new device fetches the result (`GET /link/{linkId}` →
   `{ status: "waiting" | "keyed" | "done", publicKey?, wrapped? }`, or via WebSocket message)
   and unwraps the DEK. After the first fetch with `done` the server deletes the link.

`linkId` is a UUID from the server. A wrong `code` counts towards the rate limit of the `auth`
endpoints; after 5 failed attempts for an account, its open links expire.

Only devices of the same account may complete a link.

- All `/link` endpoints need a session. Unknown, expired and foreign links all return
  `not_found`. The server normalizes the entered `code` (see 1).
- `publicKey` must be a valid P-256 point, `wrapped` exactly 60 bytes, otherwise
  `bad_request`. `key` and `complete` respond `204`, a second `complete`: `conflict`.
  `complete` (and another `key`) with a different `publicKey` than at `key`: `conflict`. The
  new device aborts if `publicKey` changes between `keyed` and `done`.
- The WebSocket message `link` goes to all devices of the account; the new device recognizes
  its `linkId`.

## 7. WebSocket

`GET /ws?token=…`. Messages from the server, JSON with a field `type` and the fields next to
it, e.g. `{"type":"changed","latestSeq":42,"deviceId":"…"}`:

| Type | Content | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `hello` | `{ latestSeq }` | After connecting. |
| `changed` | `{ latestSeq, deviceId }` | New records. The client pulls via `pull`. |
| `revoked` | `{}` | This device is revoked. The server closes afterwards. |
| `link` | `{ linkId }` | Device link completed. |

The client sends `{"type":"ping"}` every 30 seconds. Without a ping for 90 seconds the server
closes. On disconnect the client reconnects with backoff (1 s to 60 s).

- Invalid token: normal error response (`401`) instead of an upgrade. Foreign origin: `403`.
- `changed` goes to all devices of the account, also to the device that pushed (`deviceId`
  shows it). `latestSeq` is the `seq` of the last record in the push.
- Every client message counts as a ping (max. 1 KB). Close codes: `1008` after `revoked`,
  `1013` if the device is more than 16 messages behind (reconnect, then `pull`).

## 8. Protection

- Rate limits per IP for all `auth` endpoints (e.g. 10 per minute), per account for `push`.
- Maximum sizes as above. At most 10 devices and 20 passkeys per account.
- Logs without tokens, without ciphertext, without IPs longer than 7 days.

Code lookup of the link as `GET /link/by-code/{code}`, to tell it apart from the path with `linkId`. Recovery key with 4 instead of 1 check characters (36 characters = 9 groups of four, 20 bits of error detection). |

| 2026-11-23 | Instead of `gone` for `after` > `latestSeq`, new code `server_restored` (410): the device uploads everything (operator's decision). |
| 2026-11-23 | `DELETE /account`: `204`, `revoked` to all devices. |
